The Swiss Alps offer some of the most rewarding hiking in the world, with trail networks that connect quiet valley villages to dramatic high-altitude passes.

## Planning your route

Most visitors base themselves in a valley town like Zermatt, Grindelwald, or Interlaken, then take a cable car partway up before setting off on foot. This cuts hours off the climb and leaves more time for the scenery.

## The Eiger Trail

The Eiger Trail runs beneath the north face of the mountain, offering close-up views of one of the most famous rock walls in climbing history. It's a moderate hike, but the exposure to the cliffs above makes it feel far more dramatic than the elevation gain would suggest.

## Five Lakes Walk

Near Zermatt, the Five Lakes Walk links a series of alpine tarns, each offering a different reflection of the Matterhorn depending on the light and the wind.

Pack layers no matter the season — weather in the high Alps can shift from sunny to freezing within the span of an afternoon, and huts along the main routes are spaced generously enough that you'll want a plan for shelter either way.
